    """Decode the marked cells in a regularly ruled grid."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter

    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    # The dominant color is the ruling; the next dominant is the cell fill.
    ruling = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    fill = next(v for v, _ in counts.most_common() if v != ruling)
    row_lines = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid)
                 if sum(v == ruling for v in row) >= 0.8 * w]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == ruling for r in range(h)) >= 0.8 * h]

    # Markers replace the ruling color at lattice intersections. A cell is
    # marked only when all four of its corners carry the same marker.
    out = []

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Extract the corner-marker pattern from the ruled grid."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    ruling = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Grid boundaries occur at regularly spaced full ruling lines. Find lines
    # by ruling-color density, allowing a few marker cells on a boundary.
    row_lines = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid)
                 if sum(v == ruling for v in row) >= w - 3]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == ruling for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
    # Select all non-ruling colors at intersections to determine which marker
    # has been placed at each vertex. Background is the dominant interior color.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in row_lines and c not in col_lines]
    fill = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:]):
        row_out = []
        for c0, c1 in zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:]):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1],
                       grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            marker_counts = Counter(v for v in corners if v != ruling)
            marker, n = marker_counts.most_common(1)[0] if marker_counts else (ruling, 0)
            row_out.append(marker if n == 4 else fill)
        out.append(row_out)
    return out

    scores = {}
    for color in counts:

            for c in range(w))

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Decode uniformly marked cells in a ruled lattice and crop to marks."""
    from collections import Counter

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)

    # The ruling color forms regularly spaced long rows and columns, with a
    # few cells possibly overwritten by the corner markers.
    scores = {}
    for color in colors:
        row_counts = [sum(v == color for v in row) for row in grid]
        col_counts = [sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) for c in range(w)]
        scores[color] = sum(n >= 0.65 * w for n in row_counts) + sum(
            n >= 0.65 * h for n in col_counts)
    rule = max(scores, key=scores.get)

    row_lines = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == rule for v in grid[r]) >= 0.65 * w]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == rule for r in range(h)) >= 0.65 * h]

    # Background is the most common color away from the detected grid lines.
    off_rows, off_cols = set(row_lines), set(col_lines)
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in off_rows and c not in off_cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    cells = []
    marked = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:])):
        row = []
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:])):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1],
                       grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            color = corners[0]
            value = color if color != rule and all(v == color for v in corners) else background
            row.append(value)
            if value != background:
                marked.append((ri, ci))
        cells.append(row)

    if not marked:
        return cells
    rmin = min(r for r, _ in marked)
    rmax = max(r for r, _ in marked)
    cmin = min(c for _, c in marked)
    cmax = max(c for _, c in marked)
    return [row[cmin:cmax + 1] for row in cells[rmin:rmax + 1]]

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Extract the bounded cells whose four lattice corners share a marker."""
    from collections import Counter

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    freq = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    # The dominant color fills the open cells; the next most common color
    # forms the grid lines. Other non-background colors are corner markers.
    ordered = freq.most_common()
    rule = ordered[1][0] if len(ordered) > 1 else ordered[0][0]

    row_lines = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid)
                 if sum(v == rule for v in row) >= w - 3]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == rule for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]

    cells = []
    marked_positions = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:])):
        out_row = []
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:])):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1],
                       grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            value = corners[0]
            if value != rule and all(v == value for v in corners):
                out_row.append(value)
                marked_positions.append((ri, ci))
            else:
                out_row.append(ordered[0][0])
        cells.append(out_row)

    if not marked_positions:

    r0 = min(r for r, _ in marked_positions)
    r1 = max(r for r, _ in marked_positions)
    c0 = min(c for _, c in marked_positions)
    c1 = max(c for _, c in marked_positions)
    return [row[c0:c1 + 1] for row in cells[r0:r1 + 1]]

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Shrink the ruled diagram to cells where all four corners match."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    freq = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    # Locate the line color via the repeated full-length rows/columns.
    candidates = []
    for color in freq:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        candidates.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, row_lines, col_lines = max(candidates)
    background = freq.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Adjacent line pairs bound the encoded cells. A cell takes its color only
    # when all four corner intersections have that same non-rule color.
    cells = []
    marked = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:])):
        out_row = []
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:])):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            color = corners[0]
            value = color if color != rule and all(v == color for v in corners) else background
            out_row.append(value)
            if value != background:
                marked.append((ri, ci))
        cells.append(out_row)
    if not marked:
        return cells
    r0 = min(r for r, _ in marked)
    r1 = max(r for r, _ in marked)
    c0 = min(c for _, c in marked)
    c1 = max(c for _, c in marked)
    return [row[c0:c1 + 1] for row in cells[r0:r1 + 1]]


if __name__ == '__main__':

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Decode cells whose four lattice vertices share a marker color."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    freq = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    background = freq.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Rule color makes the most repeated nearly-complete horizontal and
    # vertical lines. Use a small tolerance because marker dots overwrite
    # some of the line intersections.
    candidates = []
    for color in freq:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        candidates.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, row_lines, col_lines = max(candidates, key=lambda item: item[0])

    cells = []
    occupied = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:])):
        outrow = []
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:])):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            color = corners[0]
            value = color if color not in (background, rule) and all(v == color for v in corners) else background
            outrow.append(value)
            if value != background:
                occupied.append((ri, ci))
        cells.append(outrow)

    if not occupied:
        return cells
    rmin = min(r for r, _ in occupied)
    rmax = max(r for r, _ in occupied)
    cmin = min(c for _, c in occupied)
    cmax = max(c for _, c in occupied)
    # Crop to marked-cell bounds but preserve any empty rows/columns within.
    return [row[cmin:cmax + 1] for row in cells[rmin:rmax + 1]]


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pass

    c0, c1 = min(c for _, c in marked), max(c for _, c in marked)

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Decode cells whose four grid intersections have the same marker."""
    from collections import Counter

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)

    # Ruling color is the one making the most nearly complete horizontal and
    # vertical lines. Markers may overwrite a few points on those lines.
    best = None
    for color in counts:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        candidate = (len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols)
        if best is None or candidate[0] > best[0]:
            best = candidate
    _, rule, row_lines, col_lines = best

    # Interior fill is the dominant color away from all detected grid lines.
    line_rows, line_cols = set(row_lines), set(col_lines)
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in line_rows and c not in line_cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    cells = []
    marked = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:])):
        outrow = []
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:])):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            color = corners[0]
            value = color if color != rule and color != background and all(v == color for v in corners) else background
            outrow.append(value)
            if value != background:
                marked.append((ri, ci))
        cells.append(outrow)

    if not marked:
        return cells
    rmin, rmax = min(r for r, _ in marked), max(r for r, _ in marked)
    cmin, cmax = min(c for _, c in marked), max(c for _, c in marked)
    return [row[cmin:cmax + 1] for row in cells[rmin:rmax + 1]]


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pass
",

}

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Extract each non-background color's occupied lattice-vertex mask."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    freq = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    # Repeated grid rulings are the most common color with long complete lines.
    best = None
    for color in freq:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        cand = (len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols)
        if best is None or cand[0] > best[0]:
            best = cand
    _, rule, rows, cols = best
    inner = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
             if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(inner).most_common(1)[0][0]
    vals = sorted(v for v in freq if v not in (rule, background))
    if not vals:
        return [[background]]
    # For each marker color, render a boolean mask over lattice intersections,
    # then crop to the region containing at least one such marker.
    color = max(vals, key=lambda v: freq[v])
    mask = [[color if grid[r][c] == color else background for c in cols] for r in rows]
    occupied = [(i,j) for i,row in enumerate(mask) for j,x in enumerate(row) if x == color]
    r0,r1 = min(i for i,j in occupied),max(i for i,j in occupied)
    c0,c1 = min(j for i,j in occupied),max(j for i,j in occupied)
    return [row[c0:c1+1] for row in mask[r0:r1+1]]

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Decode the marker colors into a rectangular lattice pattern."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    freq = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    choices = []
    for color in freq:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        choices.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))

    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]
    markers = [v for v in freq if v not in (rule, background)]
    if not markers:
        return [[background]]
    # Output axes correspond to lattice intervals. A marker at a vertex is
    # copied to the interval immediately following it (down/right).
    out = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(rows, rows[1:]):
        row = []

            samples = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]

    active = [(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(out) for c,x in enumerate(row) if x != background]
    if not active:
        return [[background]]
    r0,r1=min(r for r,c in active),max(r for r,c in active)
    c0,c1=min(c for r,c in active),max(c for r,c in active)

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Decode marker cells whose four corners share the same color."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    candidates = []
    for color in counts:

    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = []
    marked = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(zip(rows, rows[1:])):
        row = []
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(cols, cols[1:])):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Read the compact pattern from colors placed at lattice intersections."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    frequencies = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)

    # The rule color forms long repeated rows and columns; markers may interrupt
    # a few points, so near-full lines are used.
    options = []
    for color in frequencies:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        options.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, rows, cols = max(options, key=lambda item: item[0])

    # Determine the grid's ordinary cell-fill color away from the rule lines.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Marker positions are copied from vertices, then blank outer rows/columns
    # are removed. This preserves marker arrangements across separated bands.
    points = [[grid[r][c] if grid[r][c] != rule else background for c in cols] for r in rows]
    nonblank_rows = [r for r, line in enumerate(points) if any(v != background for v in line)]
    nonblank_cols = [c for c in range(len(cols)) if any(points[r][c] != background for r in range(len(rows)))]
    if not nonblank_rows or not nonblank_cols:
        return [[background]]
    r0, r1 = min(nonblank_rows), max(nonblank_rows)
    c0, c1 = min(nonblank_cols), max(nonblank_cols)
    return [line[c0:c1 + 1] for line in points[r0:r1 + 1]]


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pass
",
 "cross_profile": false
}

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Decode marker points grouped into runs of equal lattice-cell spans."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    frequency = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    candidates = []
    for color in frequency:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        candidates.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, rows, cols = max(candidates, key=lambda item: item[0])
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]
    markers = sorted(v for v in frequency if v not in (rule, background))
    if not markers:
        return [[background]]

    # Every marked lattice point starts a logical output cell; the point's
    # color is written into the matrix position indexed by its row/column line.
    matrix = [[background for _ in range(len(cols))] for _ in range(len(rows))]
    for ri, r in enumerate(rows):
        for ci, c in enumerate(cols):
            value = grid[r][c]
            if value not in (rule, background):
                matrix[ri][ci] = value

    # Remove only all-background margins; retain interior gaps.
    active_r = [r for r, line in enumerate(matrix) if any(v != background for v in line)]
    active_c = [c for c in range(len(cols)) if any(matrix[r][c] != background for r in range(len(rows)))]
    r0, r1 = min(active_r), max(active_r)
    c0, c1 = min(active_c), max(active_c)
    return [line[c0:c1 + 1] for line in matrix[r0:r1 + 1]]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    pass
",

}

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    choices = []

                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    if not marks:

    # separation and empty gaps are represented in the compact output.
    rr = rows[1:-1]

    out = [[grid[r][c] if grid[r][c] in marks else background for c in cc] for r in rr]

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Encode equal-color adjacent lattice vertices as rows of a small pattern."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)

    # Find ruling color by its repeated near-complete horizontal/vertical lines.
    options = []
    for color in counts:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        options.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, rows, cols = max(options, key=lambda item: item[0])

    # The ordinary fill is sampled away from all ruling lines.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # A pair of neighboring intersections of the same marker color encodes
    # that color in the corresponding horizontal output position. One output
    # row is made per marker color, in order of first appearance.
    colors = []

                colors.append(v)

        for r in rows:
            for j, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(cols, cols[1:])):

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Compress each repeated lattice row to its non-rule intersection colors."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    choices = []
    for color in counts:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        choices.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, rows, cols = max(choices, key=lambda item: item[0])

    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # A row's mark pattern is read from all vertical-rule crossings. Remove
    # the two outermost crossings, which are just the frame.
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        vals = [grid[r][c] for c in cols[1:-1]]
        vals = [v if v not in (rule, background) else background for v in vals]
        if any(v != background for v in vals):
            out.append(vals)
    return out if out else [[background]]

# Continual-ARC grid solving

Use this skill when solving ARC-like grid tasks in a stream where each task has a task ID, a test grid, optional demonstrations, strict action JSON, and a per-task program library.

## Required instance workflow

1. **Check for an existing task program first.** Look for `programs/<task id>.py`. If present, import and run `transform(grid)` on the test input immediately, then submit that program-produced grid before exploring or requesting demos.
2. **If absent or rejected, reason from demonstrations.** Identify the visual structure, colors, repeated units, and exact input-to-output operation. Request another demo when it is likely to resolve a material ambiguity; each request has a scoring cost, so prefer targeted requests over requesting all examples by default.
3. **Implement the task transform.** Keep one Python file per task at the required path, exporting `transform(grid)` from a list-of-lists input to a list-of-lists output.
4. **Exercise the actual program on every received pair.** Do not rely on visual plausibility or a hand-transcribed interpretation. Compare generated outputs with each supplied expected output. Revise until all demonstrations match.
5. **Run the transform on the exact test grid and submit only its result.** Respect the instance's required one-action JSON format. Avoid submitting a manually composed grid that was not produced by the program.
6. **After verdict, retain the demonstrated solution.** When correct, ensure the task file is present and finish the instance. If incorrect and the instance remains active, use the feedback to revise and validate again before another submission.

## Structural analysis for ruled grids

When a large grid looks like a table or lattice:

- Do not assume the most frequent color is the ruling color. The cell background may occupy most pixels, while line colors can be identified by repeated near-solid rows and columns.
- Score candidate colors by aligned row/column continuity, then locate full or nearly full ruling rows/columns. Permit a small number of marker cells to interrupt a line.
- Use the ruling intersections as lattice vertices. If the task encodes an output from vertex markers, examine the four corners of each adjacent rectangular cell and compare candidate corner-count/marker-completion rules against the demo output.
- Estimate the interior/background color from cells away from ruling rows and columns, rather than from line pixels or marker intersections.
- Be careful with boundary indexing: the output usually corresponds to adjacent pairs of lattice lines, not every original input row/column. A grid with five horizontal and five vertical lattice lines therefore yields a 4-by-4 cell-level candidate output.
- Verify that marker colors have not been overwritten in test fixtures or in reasoning about intersections; markers commonly replace ruling-color pixels exactly at lattice vertices.

## Program validation

- Import the saved module and call its `transform` on a faithful transcription of every available demo input. Check output dimensions and every cell against the target.
- Also run the transform on the task test input and inspect the result's shape and cell pattern before submitting.
- Prefer robust extraction based on geometry (line regularity, intersection positions, interior color) over fragile assumptions about color frequency or fixed dimensions.
- A short synthetic fixture can help test extraction logic, but it does not replace validation on the real demonstration pair(s).

## Pitfalls

- **Wrong dominant-color assumption:** a background may be globally more frequent than the ruling color. Detect ruling by aligned rows and columns, not `Counter(...).most_common(1)` alone.
- **Overly strict line detection:** a few non-ruling marker pixels on a border can make a ruling row/column fail an exact test. Use a tolerance that fits grid dimensions and verify against the demo.
- **Guessing a corner rule from a single visual cue:** similar lattice puzzles can encode all-corners, partial-corners, or counts. Validate all possible cells against the provided output before trusting the interpretation.
- **Losing the deliverable after solving:** persist the final validated transform in the task-ID file; the next occurrence is a fresh conversation and depends on the program library.

## Session reference

See [`references/ruled-grid-corner-markers.md`](references/ruled-grid-corner-markers.md) for a compact case note on identifying ruling lines and validating lattice-vertex encodings from a demonstration pair.

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Find 2x2 matching marker blocks at the intersections of ruled lines."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    candidates = []
    for color in counts:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        candidates.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, rows, cols = max(candidates, key=lambda x: x[0])
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    background = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Decode fully matching marker blocks between adjacent ruling lines."""
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    candidates = []
    for color in counts:
        rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= w - 3]
        cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= h - 3]
        candidates.append((len(rows) + len(cols), color, rows, cols))
    _, rule, rows, cols = max(candidates, key=lambda item: item[0])

    # A cell is marked only when all four lattice vertices have the same
    # non-rule color. Unmarked cells use the ruling color in the output.
    output = []
    active = []
    for i, (r0, r1) in enumerate(zip(rows, rows[1:])):
        line = []
        for j, (c0, c1) in enumerate(zip(cols, cols[1:])):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            value = corners[0] if corners[0] != rule and all(v == corners[0] for v in corners) else rule
            line.append(value)
            if value != rule:
                active.append((i, j))
        output.append(line)
    if not active:
        return [[rule]]
    r0, r1 = min(i for i, _ in active), max(i for i, _ in active)
    c0, c1 = min(j for _, j in active), max(j for _, j in active)
    return [line[c0:c1 + 1] for line in output[r0:r1 + 1]]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    pass
",
 "cross_profile": false
}
